title: Microsoft Purview: higher auto-labeling limits for SharePoint sites and simulation, plus new reporting
summary: The rollout facts, limits, commands and reporting locations are supported. Minor corrections should acknowledge conflicting Microsoft licensing guidance, clarify where the control paths stop, and reconcile the governance checklist with the controls table.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview is improving auto-labeling scale, SharePoint targeting, policy management and reporting.
claims.quote: These enhancements expand support for larger SharePoint scopes, improve policy management flexibility, and provide richer visibility into auto-labeling activity.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Learn documents simulation support for up to 20,000,000 matched files.
claims.quote: Simulation mode supports up to 20,000,000 matched files.

claims.claim: A policy matching more than 20,000,000 files in simulation cannot be turned on until it is narrowed and simulation rerun.
claims.quote: If more than this number of files are matched from an auto-labeling policy, you can't turn on the policy to apply the labels. In this case, you must reconfigure the auto-labeling policy so that fewer files are matched, and rerun simulation.

claims.claim: The 20,000,000 matched-file maximum applies only to simulation, not an already enabled labeling policy.
claims.quote: This maximum of 20,000,000 matched files applies to simulation mode only and not to an auto-labeling policy that's already turned on to apply sensitivity labels.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Why it matters
claims.claim: Service-side auto-labeling policies apply labels without user interaction.
claims.quote: Because the user doesn't interact with the labeling process, auto-labeling policies don't support recommended labeling

claims.claim: Across all policies, the tenant-wide maximum is 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per day.
claims.quote: The absolute maximum throughput is 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per tenant per day, in aggregate across all auto-labeling policies.

claims.claim: That maximum is not a guaranteed daily processing rate.
claims.quote: This ceiling isn't a guaranteed or consistently expected daily processing rate; actual throughput can be lower.

claims.claim: Separate licensing specific to these enhancements has not been published.

Opened auto-labeling, Insights, adaptive scopes and Purview service description; found general entitlements but no separate enhancement license.

claims.claim: No separate meter is published for these enhancements.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto labeling enhancements meter license; Purview auto-labeling scalability reporting enhancements separate license meter. Opened the auto-labeling, adaptive scopes, Insights and Purview service description pages; no enhancement-specific meter found.

claims.claim: A different license specifically for the new auto-labeling reports is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/purview auto-labeling Insights reporting licensing switch; Purview auto labeling enhancements meter license. Read Insights, auto-labeling and Purview service description; no different license for the new policy-level reports found.

claims.claim: The supplied notice does not mention a charge.
claims.quote: Searched: Read the full supplied MC1469958 notice for charges, pricing and billing; none are mentioned in its rollout schedule, impact, recommendations or compliance considerations.

claims.claim: Auto-labeling is unavailable in some regions because of a backend Azure dependency.
claims.quote: Auto-labeling isn't currently available in all regions because of a backend Azure dependency.

claims.claim: The Auto-labeling page is not visible in the Purview portal when a tenant cannot support auto-labeling.
claims.quote: If your tenant can't support this functionality, the Auto-labeling page isn't visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Explicit SharePoint targeting is reached from Purview through Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > Create auto-labeling policy.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. ... Select + Create auto-labeling policy.
claims.fix: The printed route is a valid entry point but stops before site selection. Add to controls[0].note and the rendered note: 'This path opens the creation wizard. Choose to apply a sensitivity label, select Custom > Custom policy, name the policy, choose a label, and complete Assign admin units. On Choose locations where you want to apply the label, use the SharePoint Included or Excluded link to select sites; policies with administrative units selected must instead use All.' The steps are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/apply-sensitivity-label-automatically#creating-an-auto-labeling-policy.

claims.claim: Security & Compliance PowerShell supports the printed Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy call to add SharePoint locations to an existing policy in test mode.
claims.quote: To add more sites to an existing auto-labeling policy: ... Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -AddSharePointLocation $spoLocations -ApplySensitivityLabel <Label> -Mode TestWithoutNotifications

claims.claim: Adaptive scopes are reached in the Purview portal at Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes. ... On the Adaptive scopes page, select + Create scope.
claims.fix: The route correctly reaches the scopes list, not the membership control. Add to controls[1].note and the rendered note: 'From Adaptive scopes, select + Create scope, keep Full directory for a SharePoint site scope, select SharePoint sites as the scope type, then select the properties and values for dynamic membership. SharePoint site adaptive scopes cannot be created with administrative units selected.' Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-adaptive-scopes#configure-adaptive-scopes.

claims.claim: Security & Compliance PowerShell supports New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy with Name, SharePointAdaptiveScopes, ApplySensitivityLabel and Mode TestWithoutNotifications to associate an existing adaptive scope.
claims.quote: associate an existing SharePoint adaptive scope with the policy by using the -SharePointAdaptiveScopes parameter (or -SharePointAdaptiveScopesException for exclusions) with New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy.

claims.claim: A role group with the Scope Manager role can create an adaptive scope.
claims.quote: Any role group with the Scope Manager role can create an adaptive scope.

claims.claim: Compliance Administrator is a built-in role group containing Scope Manager.
claims.quote: The Scope Manger role is included in the following built-in role groups: Compliance Administrator

claims.claim: Associating an adaptive scope with PowerShell replaces static site enumeration with dynamic membership rather than increasing the portal's site-selection limit.
claims.quote: This doesn't increase the portal limit; instead, it replaces static site enumeration with dynamic adaptive-scope membership.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated a separate tenant switch for the new reporting.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling scalability reporting enhancements tenant switch; site:learn.microsoft.com/purview auto-labeling Insights reporting licensing switch. Read auto-labeling and Insights pages and MC1469958; no separate reporting switch found.

claims.claim: The listed controls configure auto-labeling policy targeting rather than switching this rollout on or off.
claims.quote: To add more sites to an existing auto-labeling policy ... To target more than 1,000 SharePoint sites, associate an existing SharePoint adaptive scope with the policy

claims.claim: The governance checklist asks readers to check controls that have no corresponding controls-table rows.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Confirm that the roles you need are assigned'; 'Check whether any policy ... uses administrative units'; 'Test any enlarged policy in simulation'; 'Confirm auditing is on'. Table rows cover only explicit SharePoint selection and adaptive scopes.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullets beginning 'Confirm that the roles you need are assigned' and 'Check whether any policy in your tenant uses administrative units', and the At rollout bullets beginning 'Test any enlarged policy in simulation first' and 'Confirm auditing is on'. Keep their documented prerequisites and advice in Risk assessment; no new control rows are needed.
